title: Microsoft Fabric is Fueling Frontier Transformation
author: bogdanc

content.text:
If you haven’t already, read Arun Ulag’s Ignite blog post to learn how Microsoft is bringing together databases, analytics, and intelligent applications across Azure and Microsoft Fabric.
I am elated to be stepping into an expanded role leading Microsoft Fabric at an important moment for our customers and our data community. Organizations everywhere are moving beyond experimenting with AI and beginning to reimagine how people, applications, and agents work together. What is becoming increasingly clear to everyone is that this transformation starts with data: trusted, governed, and connected to the context of how each business operates.
Customers are moving quickly in this direction. More than 44,000 paid customers now use Microsoft Fabric, an increase of more than 50 percent year over year. More than 19,000 customers are also using Microsoft Foundry and Fabric together, connecting intelligent applications and agents to the operational, analytical, and unstructured data that powers their businesses. That momentum is exciting, but it also reinforces our responsibility to make the data foundation simpler, more open, and more useful for everyone who builds and works with it.
Today at Microsoft Ignite, we are introducing the next wave of innovation across Microsoft Fabric. These announcements bring together the broader Microsoft data story: unifying operational and analytical data, giving that data shared business context, and helping organizations turn trusted insights into action. Together, they show how Fabric is evolving to fuel Frontier Transformation through its deepening connection to Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft IQ, giving IT leaders the control they need and practitioners the tools to build what comes next.
Help every agent understand how your business works with Fabric IQ
Every organization has access to the same frontier models. What sets yours apart is the knowledge only your business has: how your processes run, how you define your metrics and how you serve your customers. That knowledge lives across documents and procedures, conversations in Microsoft 365, systems of record and the data your analysts model. Because it's scattered, every new agent starts from zero and teams keep rebuilding the same groundwork.
Today at Microsoft Ignite, we're introducing Microsoft IQ, the enterprise context management platform that helps you turn that knowledge into your own IQ. It captures and governs what your business knows, so every AI app and agent you build can reuse it. With new business plugins, available through the Frontier program, teams can bundle what they know into trusted, reusable context, skills and tools and share them across the business. Domain experts write a business plugin once, and every agent can use it.
Fabric IQ brings the meaning of your business data to Microsoft IQ. It models the entities, relationships, metrics and rules that define your business, building on the Power BI semantic models and Fabric data you run today. Agents work from the same definitions your analysts use, so answers stay consistent from one agent to the next. We’re introducing semantic views, now in preview, as the first semantic layer based on Apache Ossie open standards. With our deep heritage in semantic modeling with Power BI, we are making the unparalleled modeling power of Power BI broadly available to the data estate through this announcement. You define governed business metrics and semantics directly where your data lives in OneLake, in an open format designed for interoperability.
We're also bringing Fabric IQ to more of the places your teams work. Power BI semantic models in Microsoft Copilot are already generally available, and Fabric data agents are coming to Copilot, with general availability coming soon. Copilot Chat and Cowork users get Fabric IQ without consuming additional Copilot Credits. In Microsoft Excel, you can turn on Fabric IQ in Edit with Copilot, in preview, to query governed semantic models and build live, Fabric-connected PivotTables. New Fabric IQ connectors, also in preview, bring the same insights into ChatGPT and Claude.
Figure: Animated GIF - In Microsoft Copilot Chat, a user attaches a Fabric data agent to a prompt and gets an answer grounded in the organization's business data, combined with context from Work IQ.
"We are strongly impressed by the very detailed and actionable insights Microsoft Copilot Chat is providing on top of our Power BI semantic models. Excited to really start harvesting our Power BI footprint investments now!"
— Stijn Lioen, Global Architect Data & Analytics, Mohawk Industries
For developers, Fabric Apps is now (Generally Available), and you can embed conversational experiences powered by semantic models and Fabric data agents into your apps, in (Preview) Ontologies in Fabric IQ are now in GitHub Copilot, in preview, so the code it writes reflects how your business works. Fabric IQ MCP, now (Generally Available), connects any compatible agent or app to Fabric IQ under your existing Fabric permissions. Fabric IQ MCP and Skills for Fabric now also support data agents and ontologies, in (Preview).
IQ sharing in Fabric (Preview), now let’s organizations share ontologies with other enterprises, so business context can move across company boundaries along with the data. Partners can build an ontology once and share it with their customers, who can use that business context right away without recreating the underlying definitions. Financial Fabric, TomTom, xMentium, EY, and Sitecore are building IQ sharing in Fabric integrations, with availability coming soon.
Go deeper on Microsoft IQ: Read the Microsoft IQ launch blog post to learn how it helps organizations build, run, and continuously improve AI apps and agents.
Turn enterprise data into production-ready applications
Giving Copilot and agents a governed understanding of the business is only the beginning. The next opportunity is helping people and agents use that context to create applications that solve real business problems.
Today, Rayfin and Fabric apps are (Generally Available), making it easier for developers and agents to turn enterprise data into production-ready applications. Since launching in preview, builders have already created more than 100,000 apps, demonstrating the growing demand for faster, simpler ways to build applications grounded in business data.
Rayfin provides the open-source SDK and CLI for developers and AI agents to build and deploy applications to Microsoft Fabric. Fabric apps provide the managed application experience, with built-in backend services, enterprise data connectivity, security, and governance.
At Ignite, we are expanding these capabilities into the tools where people already work, making application development accessible to more developers, business users, and agents.
With the new Microsoft Copilot integration, rolling out in Frontier preview, business users can build apps directly in Copilot, with the option to use Fabric as the backend providing databases, storage, and data APIs. This creates a direct path from an idea developed through Copilot to a working application, without requiring users to assemble the underlying infrastructure. Apps built in Microsoft Copilot that require these advanced capabilities will consume Copilot Credits for the underlying Fabric services.
Watch Introducing Microsoft Fabric HorizonDB: Serverless PostgreSQL for Intelligent Apps and Fabric apps: Build like a startup. Deploy like an enterprise demos on YouTube.
We’re also introducing a new app building experience in Power BI Desktop, powered by Fabric apps, that enables users to create modern interactive applications using natural language. Starting from a trusted semantic model, users can generate, preview, edit, and publish purpose-built applications to Microsoft Fabric. Importantly, this experience isn’t limited to Microsoft Fabric capacity customers. Apps in Power BI will be available to Power BI Pro customers, with support for PPU in the coming months.
These applications are designed to go beyond prototypes. With access to OneLake storage and transactional database services, developers can build applications that combine enterprise data, business logic, and operational workflows.
Together, these capabilities connect the full application journey from Fabric IQ’s trusted context to AI-powered application development and enterprise-ready services. Organizations can now move faster from data and insights to application that drive action.
Build with Fabric apps: Explore the Fabric apps deep-dive and Power BI technical, blog posts, where you can find examples, availability, and guidance for getting started.
Bring operational and analytical data together with Fabric HorizonDB
Building intelligent applications requires more than analytics. Developers and AI agents need access to operational data, historical insights, and business context without stitching together separate systems or managing complex data pipelines.
Today, we are announcing the preview of Microsoft Fabric HorizonDB, a serverless, Fabric-native PostgreSQL database that brings operational data, analytics, and AI together on one governed platform. Built on the innovation behind Azure HorizonDB, now generally available, it lets developers use familiar PostgreSQL tools while connecting directly to Fabric's analytics and AI.
Fabric HorizonDB is built for the bursty demands of applications and agents. Databases provision in less than five seconds, scale automatically with demand, and cut costs with auto-pause and wake-on-query. Native integration with OneLake makes operational data available for analytics without complex ETL pipelines, while reverse ETL enables teams to bring insights back into operational applications.
With translytical queries, applications and agents no longer have to choose between live transactional data and deep analytics. A single PostgreSQL query can run scale-out analytics on Fabric Data Warehouse and join the results with live operational tables in Fabric HorizonDB, with no data movement or new query language. Paired with Fabric apps and trusted business context from Fabric IQ, teams can build, analyze, and act on data in one place instead of managing separate operational and analytical systems.
We're also announcing the general availability of Database Hub in Fabric, providing a unified experience to discover, monitor, and manage databases across Azure, Fabric, on-premises environments, and other clouds. As organizations build more applications and their database estates grow, Database Hub helps teams gain visibility into database health and performance, simplify operations, and manage their environments more efficiently.
Watch a demo of the Database Hub in Fabric in action.
And with database agents for SQL and PostgreSQL in (Preview), we're bringing AI-powered assistance directly into database operations. These agents help developers and database professionals identify performance and health issues, understand their root causes, and take recommended actions with human oversight.
Together, Fabric HorizonDB, Database Hub, and database agents help organizations move from fragmented database environments to a more connected, intelligent foundation for building and operating modern applications.
Explore the Fabric databases deep-dive blog post and tips for getting started.
Scale innovation with security and governance built-in
As organizations move agents from pilot to production, data leaders go from needing to understand what their agents are doing to trusting the work that it does and fixing it if something goes wrong. Scaling AI responsibly depends on the same visibility and controls that teams expect for their data estate.
That is why we are expanding observability in Fabric with centralized telemetry in the refreshed Monitor Hub and detailed traces available through Workspace Monitoring, helping teams detect issues, investigate their causes, and take action.
Now in preview, Observability for Fabric data and operations agents enables teams to troubleshoot agent issues where they work: in the Azure portal, in the Fabric Monitor Hub, in Foundry observability or through a coding agent using MCP or APIs. Agent traces are also available in Workspace Monitoring, with support for exporting Fabric data agent insights to Azure Monitor and Application Insights for end-to-end visibility of agents coming soon.
Together, these capabilities help organizations improve reliability, streamline troubleshooting, and scale AI-powered solutions with confidence.
OneLake as the unified and governed foundation for data and AI
As we deliver innovation across the platform, OneLake continues to be the foundation that unifies a customer’s data estate. There are several announcements we’re sharing today that further strengthen OneLake’s ability to unify and govern data for analytics and AI.
Salesforce is part of how a lot of our customers run their business, and they want that data in OneLake. Now in preview, Salesforce Data 360 customer data can be securely shared into OneLake with zero ETL and no duplication for accurate analytics and AI.
Many customers have complex, fine-grained permissions on their OneLake data, and they need those permissions to follow the data into AI. Now in preview, AI Search (Microsoft Foundry) support for OneLake with OneLake security ensures that agents and apps built on indexed OneLake data return only what each user is allowed to see, without rebuilding access controls.
For two years, customers have become accustomed to using OneLake catalog for discovering, governing, and securing data from across their entire data estate. Now, we’re taking the next step to make OneLake Catalog the focal point of Microsoft’s data governance strategy by delivering new data governance capabilities that bring data, context, and governance together for AI.
There are several other notable announcements for OneLake we’re disclosing today including features that are now generally available. For full details, please read the OneLake blog post.
A connected foundation for Frontier Transformation
The announcements we are sharing at Ignite cover different parts of Microsoft Fabric, but they address one connected challenge.
Organizations need more than access to the latest models. They need to bring together data from across the business, give it consistent meaning, and make that intelligence available to people, developers, applications, Copilot, and agents. They must also turn ideas into production experiences without rebuilding the data, backend services, security, and governance foundation for every project.
Fabric provides that connected foundation.
OneLake unifies the data estate. Fabric IQ turns business data and semantics into governed context within Microsoft IQ. Fabric apps help teams turn ideas and insights into production applications across Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Copilot. Fabric HorizonDB provides transactional data services for those applications. Integrated security and governance give administrators visibility and control as adoption grows.
Each part becomes more valuable because it is connected to the others.
This is how Microsoft Fabric helps fuel Frontier Transformation. Not by adding intelligence as a separate layer over fragmented systems, but by bringing together data, business context, analytics, application development, and governance on one platform.
We are inspired by what the Fabric community has already built, including more than 100,000 applications since the Fabric apps preview, and even more excited about what comes next. I invite you to explore the announcements at Microsoft Ignite, try the new capabilities as they become available, and share your feedback as we continue building the future of Fabric together.
Sessions not to miss at Microsoft Ignite
There is much more to explore at Microsoft Ignite. Join our Fabric sessions and labs to see these capabilities in action, hear directly from the teams building them, and learn how to put them to work across your data estate. I especially encourage you to attend INV641, BRK306, BRK351, BRK352, and BRK357, and visit the Fabric experience in the Hub to connect with our product teams and community.
Explore all our Fabric sessions: Fabric at Microsoft Ignite.
Registration is open for FabCon and SQLCon
With 2027 just around the corner, I hope you will join me and the team at FabCon and SQLCon in Atlanta, Georgia and for the first time in the Asia Pacific region in Sydney, Australia. These events are a great opportunity to go deeper on the latest innovations, learn directly from our product experts, and connect with the Fabric and SQL communities that are shaping what comes next. Register early to take advantage of the best available pricing before rates increase.
Registration links:
• FabCon & SQLCon in Atlanta, United States | March 8 – 12, 2027 | Register by December 18 for super early bird discount.
• FabCon & SQLCon in Sydney, Australia | April 6 – 9, 2027 | Register by December 15 for super early bird discount.
Explore additional Microsoft Fabric resources
• Sign up for the free Fabric trial – no credit card required.
• View the updated Fabric Roadmap.
• Find the capacity right for you with the Microsoft Fabric SKU Estimator.
• Visit the Fabric homepage.
• Join the amazing Fabric community.
• Read other in-depth, technical blog posts on the Microsoft Fabric Updates Blog.
• Read the Gartner Magic Quadrant report for Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms.
• Read the blog post announcing Microsoft’s placement in the Gartner Magic Quadrant report for Data Integration Tools.
